problem: The rate at which a pot of hot oil cools is proportional to the difference between its temperature and the temperature of its surroundings. Let $T(t)$ be the temperature of the liquid in degrees Celsius, and let $t>0$ be the time in minutes. If the temperature of the surroundings is ${30}^{∘}\text{C},$ which differential equation could be used to model the temperature of the oil? Assume that $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality.

activity_context.topic_title: Inhibited Decay Models With First-Order ODEs
